notes: The paper's 'H2 storage capacity' (e.g. 5.8 wt%, Table 2, Fig. 6) is catalytic hydrogenation of liquid N-ethylcarbazole at 200 C and 40 bar H2, quantified by GC product distribution; it is not H2 uptake by a sorbent (I1 exclusion: hydrogenation without measured uptake). The only gas-phase H2 uptake measured on the solid is Fig. 7: volumetric H2 physisorbed/chemisorbed/total isotherms (0-800 mm Hg, cc/g STP) on Pt/Ni@(N)G-18 and Pt/Ni@(N)G-0 (carbon-majority Ni/Pt on N-doped graphitic carbon, C about 72-74 wt%, Ni 14-15 wt%). No temperature is given for these isotherms in the figure, caption or text. Section 2.3 describes only pulse chemisorption (Micromeritics AutoChem II 2920, pulses of 5 vol% H2 in He after cooling to 'room temperature'); that protocol does not produce a pressure-swept isotherm, so its temperature cannot be assigned to Fig. 7, and 'room temperature' in words is unstated under the schema's temperature_unstated rule. Hence I3 fails -> no_conditions_stated. If I1 were instead judged not met (chemisorption used only as catalyst characterization), the code would still be no_conditions_stated. If 'room temperature' were accepted for Fig. 7, I4 would decide (no_surface_area), since the only area reported is a Ni metal surface area (1.78 m2/g).
